recaps.title: Own Goal FC sweep, and a hat trick decides the opener
recaps.subtitle: Two series · 6 games · 30 goals
recaps.headline: Own Goal FC opened Season 2 with a 3–0 sweep. TRS 1000 closed the other series with a hat trick.
recaps.html:
Season 2 kicked off with a doubleheader: Fortnite Flick FC vs. Bucky Irving FC, followed immediately by Own Goal FC vs. California Gurls. Both series went to the board as best-of-threes, and by the end of the night the league already had its first unbeaten team, its first winless team, and a handful of stat lines worth watching. Lawson State and 999 sat the night out on bye.

Standings after Match Day 1

Rank Team Record Win % GF GA
1 Own Goal FC 3–0 100.0% 11 5
2 Fortnite Flick FC 2–1 66.7% 11 6
3 Bucky Irving FC 1–2 33.3% 6 11
4 (tie) California Gurls 0–3 0.0% 5 11
4 (tie) Lawson State 0–0 — — —
4 (tie) 999 0–0 — — —

Own Goal FC and Fortnite Flick FC both won their series, but only OG did it clean. California Gurls take the early basement seat, having dropped all three games to a hot Own Goal FC roster.

Fortnite Flick FC def. Bucky Irving FC, 2–1

FF took the series, but it wasn't a walkover. Bucky Irving FC — built by DrewAJC as the league's only all-veteran, zero-rookie roster — made it a fight, and actually out-worked Fortnite Flick FC on the resource stats even while losing.

Game 1 — FF 4, BI 1. Fortnite Flick FC came out of the gate hot. LLellum, Season 2's marquee Grand Champion I signing, opened his RPL career with a 2-goal, 1-assist, 3-save game (728 score) — comfortably the best individual performance of the night. Sajar47 matched him goal-for-goal with a 2G/1A game of his own, and TRS 1000 chipped in an assist. Blockymalrd's lone goal was the only thing BI had to show for it.

Game 2 — BI 3, FF 2. Bucky Irving hit back immediately. drateRbmud scored twice, Blockymalrd and DrewAJC each set one up, and BI levelled the series. LLellum and TRS 1000 both scored for FF, but Sajar47 was held scoreless despite four saves — a defense-only outing sandwiched between two big offensive games.

Game 3 — FF 5, BI 2. The decider belonged to TRS 1000, who put up a 3-goal game to close the series out — the first hat trick of Season 2. Sajar47 bounced back with 2 goals and an assist. On the other side, drateRbmud kept producing (2 more goals, 4 for the series), but it wasn't enough. LLellum, notably, didn't score at all in the clincher, finishing with just an assist.

What the series says

The headline name didn't carry this one the way the price tag might suggest. LLellum's stat line shrank every game — 728 to 395 to 319 by score — while Sajar47 built the opposite trend (420, 473, 671) and finished as the series' leading scorer by total score (1,564, ahead of even LLellum's 1,442). TRS 1000's Game 3 hat trick was the series-defining moment; he ended the day a perfect 4-for-4 on goals-to-shots.

On Bucky Irving's side, DrewAJC — the manager who bet on Season 1 chemistry over rookie upside — didn't find the net once in three games, leaving the scoring to drateRbmud (4 goals) and Blockymalrd (2 goals, plus a league-high 8 demos inflicted on the day).

And BI genuinely won the physical series they lost on the scoreboard: more boost collected, more boost stolen, and a lopsided 12-to-1 demo count in their favour. All of that hustle produced one game. It's a small early lesson in what the raw activity numbers do and don't predict.

Own Goal FC def. California Gurls, 3–0

This one was never really close. Own Goal FC — built by first-time manager Bl4zeDaddy around a proven veteran (TLBoryczka at $12,591) plus a cheap flier (Spam God6450 at $3,025) — looked exactly like a team that spent to win now.

Game 1 — OG 2, CG 1. Bl4zeDaddy and TLBoryczka each scored once for OG. Jart's goal was California Gurls' only answer. Ugadawg50, the cheapest buy of the Season 2 auction at $900, had the roughest game of the night with a 74 score.

Game 2 — OG 6, CG 3. Spam God6450 exploded for a 3-goal game, with Bl4zeDaddy and TLBoryczka (2 goals) also finding the net. California Gurls got goals from all three players — F1yTe Bacon, Jart and Ugadawg50 — but couldn't keep pace.

Game 3 — OG 3, CG 1. More of the same. Bl4zeDaddy, Spam God6450 and TLBoryczka each scored once more to close it out, with only F1yTe Bacon answering for CG.

What the series says

Bl4zeDaddy quietly had the most consistent line in the league on opening night — a goal in all three games, plus 2 assists, and zero saves recorded across the entire series. That's not a weakness so much as a role: Own Goal FC's captain played pure attack and let TLBoryczka handle the two-way work. He finished with 4 goals, 2 assists, and all three of OG's team saves — the same complete profile that made him the league's assist leader in Season 1.

Spam God6450's Game 2 hat trick is worth flagging against his Season 1 record: a 7-game outlier whose numbers were voided when his team was pulled from competition. One hot game isn't proof, but it's the kind of game those numbers predicted.

On the losing side, F1yTe Bacon was quietly California Gurls' best player in defeat — 2 goals, 2 assists, 5 saves across the sweep, present in all three losses without ever getting much help.

Team by team

Own Goal FC (3–0). The night's best team by any measure: 11 goals for, 5 against, achieved while spending the least time in their own defensive third (43.8%) and the most in the opponent's attacking third (22.6%) of anyone who played. Strikingly, they logged only 4 saves in three games, fewest of any team — not because their defense was bad, but because they mostly didn't need it. The one caution flag: they also led the league in time sitting at full boost (529.8 seconds), arguably wasted resource. It didn't cost them anything against this opponent.

Fortnite Flick FC (2–1). Took the series but were the more inefficient team underneath. Their star signing tailed off across three games even as the series was won. The real story here is Sajar47 and TRS 1000 stepping up, not LLellum running away with it.

Bucky Irving FC (1–2). Lost the series despite winning almost every resource battle: most boost collected (23,205) and stolen (4,316) of any team, the highest boost BPM (418, i.e. the busiest team on the field), and that 12-to-1 demo count. Worth watching whether the gap between activity and results closes as an all-veteran roster settles in, or whether it's a real finishing problem.

California Gurls (0–3). A rough opening night across the board: the most time spent at zero boost of any team (583.5s), the least time in the attacking third (14.7%), and the fewest boost steals (1,936). The numbers point to a team that lost the territorial and resource battle, not just the scoreline. F1yTe Bacon's individual output is the bright spot to build from.

Lawson State and 999. On bye. First appearances still to come.

Standouts

Best individual game — LLellum, Game 1: 2 goals, 1 assist, 3 saves, 728 score. The best box score of the night, even if his production curve went the other way from there.

Best series — TLBoryczka, Own Goal FC: 4 goals, 2 assists, 3 saves across a 3–0 sweep, and the only OG player with a save in every game.

Biggest moment — TRS 1000's 3-goal Game 3. Bucky Irving had just levelled the series at 1–1; he ended it, and finished the night converting every shot he took.

Quiet reversal — DrewAJC didn't score once in three games. His Season 1 numbers already showed an unusually low assist rate for a returning veteran; worth watching whether opening night was a fluke or the start of a pattern in a bigger role.

Value watch — Ugadawg50, the cheapest buy of the auction at $900, posted the softest individual series of the day and the night's lowest single-game score. One match day is one match day, but it tracks with a Season 1 sample that was already the league's thinnest.

Territorial figures such as time-in-third are ballchasing.com proxies, not literal possession — the underlying data doesn't track ball touches directly.
